items.summary:
In early trading, the Nvidia news affected almost no other stocks. The Nasdaq 100, which tracks the top tech stocks at the Nasdaq exchange, soared 3%. The broader S&P 500 2%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose almost 900 points. Stocks were also propelled higher by a sharp 5% drop in oil prices on Monday, on news that U.S. and Iran talks were continuing. Trump also told CNN on Sunday that it would be “highly unlikely” that he would restart major combat operations against Iran. [...] “A committee of independent directors, assisted by outside independent counsel, will oversee the investigation,” Nvidia said in a Sunday statement. “The Board prioritizes U.S. national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders.”

An Nvidia spokesperson told NBC News that Huang was “committed to continuing to lead NVIDIA as CEO without interruption.” [...] By Steve Kopack and Rob Wile

Nvidia’s stock slid about 4% on Monday after the company announced that it had opened an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang’s relationship with a woman that U.S. intelligence agencies say is a Chinese spy.

The probe has the potential to unsettle the entire AI boom, fueled by trillions of dollars of spending and investments, in part to purchase Nvidia’s cutting-edge AI chips. Nvidia’s drop wiped out more than $200 billion in value.

Tesla, Inc., headquartered in Austin, Texas, is an American manufacturer of electric automobiles, solar panels, and batteries for cars and home power storage. It was founded in 2003 by American entrepreneurs Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning and was named after Serbian American inventor Nikola Tesla. It quickly became one of the most recognizable car brands in the world.

## Tesla’s business segments [...] Although Tesla is best known for its electric vehicles, it also produces energy-storage systems and technology products. Its business is divided into two segments: automotive; and energy generation and storage.

### Automotive [...] Tesla Motors was formed to develop an electric sports car. Eberhard was Tesla’s chief executive officer (CEO) and Tarpenning its chief financial officer (CFO). Funding for the company was obtained from a variety of sources, most notably PayPal cofounder Elon Musk, who contributed more than $30 million to the new venture and served as chair of the company beginning in 2004.

items.title: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production after years of poor sales in few markets
items.summary:
By Reuters

Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production at its Texas gigafactory around mid-2027, CEO Elon Musk said on Friday, after years of persistently weak sales for a futuristic model once touted as a rival to legacy pickup trucks that ultimately only sold in just a handful of markets because of its heavy, angular design. [...] The Cybercab, which has butterfly doors and no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors, is one of Musk's key bets in his push to turn Tesla into an AI and robotics company rather than just an automaker.

Musk has said he sees it as Tesla's main autonomous model supplying a global network of robotaxis. [...] In response to a user on X, Musk called the Cybertruck the "best vehicle Tesla has ever made" and the wind-down the "end of an era."

Tesla did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment sent outside regular business hours.

args.text:
Dưới đây là hàm Python đơn giản để đảo ngược một chuỗi:

```python
def reverse_string(s: str) -> str:
    return s[::-1]

# Ví dụ sử dụng:
text = "Xin chào"
print(reverse_string(text))  # Kết quả: "oàhc niX"
```
